source: synthesis of 4 area audits, every HIGH/MEDIUM gap re-verified by reading cited code on main @ dceea03a (read-only worktree /home/kali/vigil-wt-apex-audit)
note: All 5 APEX PRs are MERGED and in main. Everything below is default-OFF and undriven in the shipped config. No code was modified by this audit.

items.name: APEX enablement path in deploy env + runbook
items.what: Add every APEX flag (autonomous, oob, impact, presentation, consumer surfaces) to customer.env.example + cockpit.env.example (identical on both planes), to OWNER-SWITCHES.md, and an APEX enablement page in GO-LIVE-quickstart.md. Today there is NO supported way to turn APEX on.
items.owner_input: Decide which APEX layers launch (engine autonomy / OOB-first / impact-closure) and which consumer surfaces (posture, attack-path, blind-vuln, retest).
items.verified: CONFIRMED — grep VIGIL_APEX over all *.env.example, infra/systemd/*, docs/runbooks/* returns zero hits.

items.name: Production driver for PCR close-the-loop
items.what: Build a sovereign CLI subcommand + systemd/worker that injects governance signers, GitHub App material, the m-of-n destruction quorum and the patched-build redrive into remediation.apex_pcr.close_remediation_loop, so a confirmed FACT drives a gated fix PR + signed negative certificate. Today the capability is a library with no caller outside tests.
items.owner_input: Supply target repo/branch + governance signer quorum; approve opening real fix PRs (m-of-n), since the PR leg touches a target repo.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — grep close_remediation_loop: only its own def + __all__ in apex_pcr.py; zero callers in cli.py/jobs/ui.

items.name: Production ticker for continuous retest scheduler
items.what: Add a cadence job (systemd oneshot+timer mirroring vigil-reprove) that loads a persisted RetestRegistry, populates it from confirmed findings, injects redpen_fix.refire_reproduction as refire, calls jobs.apex_retest_scheduler.run_cadence_tick on a cadence, and surfaces reopened findings to the operator. Today nothing ticks it.
items.owner_input: Decide the cadence and where the registry file lives; approve enabling the timer and VIGIL_APEX_IMPACT.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — grep run_cadence_tick: zero non-test callers; the existing vigil-reprove.timer drives a different (TRUTHENOVATION A2) path.

items.name: Provision a public OOB collector host
items.what: Stand up a public TLS reverse proxy fronting the loopback relay (advertise_url); an owner-owned domain delegated (NS) to the DNS collector bound on routable :53; set CRUCIBLE_OOB_RELAY_SECRET + LiveConfig oob_enable/oob_relay_host/oob_advertise_base_url; run the owner-signed `vigil provision` to pin the collector pubkey into the engagement authority; write an OOB-collector runbook. Without it, every blind-SSRF/SSTI claim fail-closes to a LEAD.
items.owner_input: Provide the public collector host, a dedicated DNS name + delegated base domain, open :53 and the TLS port, and run the governance-signed provision ceremony. (The plan already names this as an owner input, but it is not in any deploy artifact or runbook.)
items.verified: CONFIRMED — oob_collaborator.py:14-26 '127.0.0.1 ONLY', remote arm GUIDE-ONLY; dns_collector.py needs an owner-owned nameserver; no deploy/runbook coverage.

items.name: Unify the VIGIL_APEX_IMPACT flag reader
items.what: Make sigil.config.apex_impact_enabled delegate to vigil_integration.apex_flags.apex_impact_enabled (one shared reader, fail-closed on ImportError), OR align the truthy sets. Today the sovereign reader accepts 'enabled' (5-element set) while the engine + integration readers do not (4-element set), so VIGIL_APEX_IMPACT=enabled reads ON on one plane, OFF on the other. Latent now (no live sovereign caller); becomes a real split the moment the sovereign reader is wired.
items.owner_input: Decide whether to land the consumer-E fix or patch the divergence directly on main before any sovereign-plane consumer ships.
items.covered_by_running_work: YES — the written fix exists on an unmerged commit (e093e163) that is part of the consumer-E fix round. Landing that round closes this.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — config.py:1248 _OIDC_AFFIRMATIVE has 'enabled'; apex_flags.py:15 and apex_impact.py:37 _TRUTHY do not; config.apex_impact_enabled has no live caller on main.

items.name: Driver resume durability
items.what: On --resume the autonomous driver is skipped (no open executor) and its oracle-confirmed findings are never re-persisted (report is persisted at scan-complete, before the driver folds its findings), so a resumed run loses them. Either re-snapshot the report after the driver folds, or re-run the driver over a reopened executor, or explicitly document the driver as non-resumable.
items.owner_input: Decide the intended resume semantics: recover-and-skip (re-persist), re-run on resume, or documented non-resumable.
items.verified: CONFIRMED (code path) — engage.py:1994-1997 skips the driver on resume; persist_report at :1965 only (scan-complete), no re-persist after the driver block. Runtime loss is INFERRED from the code, not re-executed.

items.name: Owner-gated customer-path driver wiring
items.what: The customer launch worker reaches run_engagement, but the flag is wired into no deploy env / UI / launch gate, and the separate live/engine.py 'unified OODA engine' never runs the APEX driver. If hosted customers should ever run it, add explicit owner-gated deploy-env + launch-gate wiring (consistent with VIGIL_CUSTOMER_PROD_EXECUTION) and a test. Otherwise document the operator/CLI-only boundary.
items.owner_input: Confirm whether PR-1 is operator/CLI-only for now, or whether hosted customers should run the autonomous driver (owner-gated at go-live).
items.verified: CONFIRMED — engage_worker.py:456-460 _default_run_engagement->run_engagement; live/engine.py:258-272 is a separate engine; no VIGIL_APEX wiring in deploy/custui.

items.name: Widen the autonomous discovery arsenal
items.what: The in-band discovery probe is 5 near-zero-FP checks (XSS/open-redirect/path-traversal/SSTI x2). SQLi is excluded (single-shot FP) and OOB (SSRF/XXE/RCE) self-skips without a receiver. So injection/ssrf-oob/auth/access-control/business-logic/exploit-chain only get exercised on REVERIFY of scan findings, not fresh discovery. Add SPRT-gated boolean-SQLi discovery and OOB discovery (once AP04 lands) to light up the starved surface domains.
items.owner_input: Confirm the intended division of labor: PR-1 discovers only the 5 in-band classes; OOB/SQLi discovery arrives via PR-2 provisioning + future SPRT work.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — builtin.py:213-236 curated_probe_checks returns exactly 5 checks; SQLi + OOB deliberately excluded (documented).

items.name: Wire the in-engagement live-impact arm for authorized prod
items.what: engage calls pursue_impact with no gate and no live_prover, so in production chaining-to-impact is offline oracle re-fire only; the live data-access/privesc/ATO demonstration runs only in tests. If live impact pursuit is intended in prod, add an authorized prod-execution caller that injects build_offense_gate + a real live_prover; otherwise state explicitly that in-engagement impact is offline-re-fire-only.
items.owner_input: Owner approval + prod-execution authority (VIGIL_CUSTOMER_PROD_EXECUTION + signed charter) before any live impact pursuit touches a target.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — engage.py:2049-2053 calls pursue_impact with no gate=/live_prover=; apex_impact.py:170-172 takes the live arm only when both are injected.

items.name: Reconcile Gate-5 sign-off with the shipped config
items.what: The owner's Gate-5 E2E walk turns the presentation surfaces ON (posture + presentation; attack-path/blind-vuln), but customer.env.example ships them OFF, so a green Gate-5 does not reflect what the hosted launch serves. Either ship the surfaces on (set the flags in both env files) and re-run Gate-5 against the real go-live env, or scope Gate-5 to the shipped (off) config.
items.owner_input: Confirm whether Fix-first / Attack-path / Retest are part of the launch surface.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — test_gate5_customer_e2e.py:167,177 enables posture/attackPath/blindVuln/VIGIL_APEX_PRESENTATION; customer.env.example has none of them.

items.name: Master VIGIL_APEX_ENABLED kill-switch (or record the decision)
items.what: Appendix Z specified a master VIGIL_APEX_ENABLED (default OFF) ANDed into each sub-flag. It was never implemented; only independent sub-flags exist, so there is no single off-switch for the whole program. Either implement it or update the plan to record that the design settled on independent sub-flags.
items.owner_input: Confirm whether a single master kill-switch is wanted for operations.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — grep VIGIL_APEX_ENABLED across .py/.md/.example returns zero hits.

items.name: Refresh V2-LIMITATIONS and add an APEX residuals section
items.what: V2-LIMITATIONS.md section 31 still calls the nosqli/ldap/xpath datastore_error branches 'LEAD-only (fact_capable: false)', but #1182 promoted them to fact_capable=true via the parser-state-toggle oracle. Rewrite section 31, and add an APEX residuals section (public-collector provisioning, test-only PCR/retest drivers, flag divergence) so an auditor is not misled.
items.verified: CONFIRMED — V2-LIMITATIONS.md:1407-1442 says LEAD-only; evidence-branches.json:2261/2319/2377 all fact_capable=true.

items.name: Render impact_report in reports/UI
items.what: EngagementResult.impact_report is computed but surfaced nowhere — no report renderer or UI consumes it, so the demonstrated-impact deliverable is invisible to the operator. Render demonstrated paths, terminal_impact, foothold_findings and authorization in the technical/engagement report and/or a UI panel.
items.verified: Reported by area audit (grep: only producer, no reader). Not independently re-verified beyond the audit grep — LOW.

items.name: Range-backed MERIDIAN e2e acceptance
items.what: The committed PR-1 e2e acceptance runs against a loopback pytest_httpserver, not the MERIDIAN range the plan names. The promote->crawl->probe->oracle chain is faithful and the capability is demonstrated end-to-end on an equivalent target. Add a MERIDIAN-range-backed e2e, or amend the plan to accept the loopback-equivalent as the acceptance surface.
items.owner_input: Confirm whether the loopback-equivalent is an acceptable stand-in for the MERIDIAN acceptance, or a range-backed e2e is required.
items.verified: Reported by area audit (test header 'Loopback pytest_httpserver only'). LOW.

items.name: Reconcile customer-facing copy with shipped flags
items.what: Add when-gates to the in-app Guide steps (attackpath/retest/OOB-badge) so the Guide matches the served surface, and review public-site 'autonomous pentesting engine' / 'verified fix suggestions' copy against the shipped defaults. Either enable the capabilities or soften the copy (e.g. 'autonomous OODA available / opt-in').
items.owner_input: None if the flags are enabled; otherwise approve the one-line guide gating fix + copy softening.
items.verified: Reported by area audit (guide.js steps lack when-gates; public_site/index.html claims). LOW.

new_or_corrections.summary: VIGIL_APEX_MAX_CYCLES is an APEX env flag omitted from the §3 flag table.
new_or_corrections.detail: Read at engage.py:120 (_apex_max_cycles), default 64 (_APEX_MAX_CYCLES_DEFAULT, engage.py:104), operator-tunable OODA-cycle bound. Only mentioned in checklist step 7. AP01 must enumerate it in the env for a reproducible runaway-loop bound.

new_or_corrections.summary: Two APEX consumer surfaces missing from the §3 consumer-flag row: VIGIL_CUSTOMER_PROOF_BADGE (APEX PR-I) and VIGIL_CUSTOMER_FIX_IT.
new_or_corrections.detail: PROOF_BADGE renders the 'Independently verifiable' per-finding badge + proof-bundle download (placeholder __VIGIL_PROOF_BADGE__ custui.py:276; route /api/customer/assessments/proof gated at server.py:726). FIX_IT (config.py:301) is the one-click gated fix-PR + signed NEGATIVE remediation cert button (the consumer trigger for close-the-loop; offense side re-checks VIGIL_REDPEN_ENABLED + owner-signed 'pr' grant, mints no fact). Both default OFF.

new_or_corrections.summary: PROOF_BADGE IS present (commented, OFF) in both env examples; the blanket 'no presentation flag in any deploy env' is not exact. H1 still stands (its literal claim is 0 VIGIL_APEX_ hits; PROOF_BADGE is VIGIL_CUSTOMER_).

Verified all four APEX flags both planes: AUTONOMOUS (engage.py:103), OOB (runtime_redrive.py:391) and PRESENTATION (certify.py:191) all use the 5-value set matching sovereign _OIDC_AFFIRMATIVE. Only IMPACT's _TRUTHY (apex_flags.py:15, apex_impact.py:37) is 4-value. So M1 is correctly isolated to IMPACT, and IMPACT's ENGINE reader is the family outlier — the lowest-risk AP05 fix is to bring _TRUTHY UP to 5 values (add 'enabled'), not down-scope config.

The PCR and retest libraries are NOT 'proven by one hermetic test each' — test_apex_pcr.py has 9 tests and test_apex_retest_scheduler.py has 8, with real negative controls (quorum-blocks, patched-build-not-certified, no-false-clear). H2/H3 (no production caller) are unchanged; the libraries are better-proven than §2 states.

The APEX consumer screens are server-rendered in custui.py via __VIGIL_*__ placeholder substitution (__VIGIL_POSTURE__/RETEST/ATTACK_PATH/BLIND_VULN/PROOF_BADGE at custui.py:267-278) + route gates in server.py (/posture @1818, /proof @726). customer_app/app.js carries ZERO APEX content — citing it (M3/L5) points at the wrong file. Conclusion (surfaces default-OFF) unchanged; review target for L5 is custui.py.
